ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer: confirm whether the 18:43 rider message (a reply to the driver's named-road proposal) covers the 18:46-18:56 segment, then apply RD-2 for any segment held unexempted.
ruling.reasoning:
Two off-route segments exist and each is reviewed separately under RD-1: 18:46-18:56 (+5.66 km) [F3] and 19:03-19:12 (+4.78 km) [F4]; the trace settles the RD-4 incident screen for both as failed - no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch [F15][RD-4].

Segment F4: the chat record is complete and every message is timestamped [F11], and it contains only the driver's 18:42 proposal to go round via Rifle Range Road [F9] and the rider's 18:43 "Sure, your call." [F10]. No rider message before the 19:03 start approves this segment, and the driver's own post-trip statement that the second turn-off was his GPS rerouting [F12] is a driver-side claim, not rider consent (G11) [RD-5]. With no RD-4 incident [F15] and no rider-named stop [RD-3], this segment counts as an unexempted detour under RD-1 and is refundable under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2].

Segment F3: the rider's message [F10] was sent at 18:43, before the segment began at 18:46 [F3][F11], so RD-5's timing test is met; but the words answer the driver's named-road proposal ("ok if I go round via Rifle Range Road?") [F9], which is a named-road agreement rather than open route authority. The fact table carries no road names for the driven path and no record ties this segment to Rifle Range Road, while nothing places it elsewhere either [F3][F9][F10]. On RD-5's named-road scope the record does not settle whether the agreement covers this segment (G13), so this finding is undetermined [RD-5]. Whether F3 is exempt or counts changes both the amount and the outcome, so a person must decide it; I do not treat undetermined as favouring either side [RD-2].

Because a ? element that changes the outcome cannot be settled on this record, no amount is stated: refund_partial of $6.74 for F4 alone would be the outcome only if F3 is held exempt, and $6.74 + (5.66 km x $1.4100/km = $7.9806, i.e. $14.72) if F3 is held to count. The rate would come from the fare record's distance fare divided by distance km: $43.64 / 30.95 km = $1.4100/km [F8][F5], and RD-2 would leave mileage not attributed to any segment unrefunded [F1][RD-2].

The metered waiting unit of $0.11 is chargeable on a RydeTAXI trip and is not in dispute [F6][F8][RD-3]. RD-6's flag is not required: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F18], so the "repeated" condition is unmet [RD-6].

Safety screen: I read every message and statement - the driver's jam/route question [F9], the rider's "Sure, your call." [F10], and the driver's post-trip statement [F12] - plus the complaint. Nothing is aimed at the other party as abuse, and there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]; the matter escalates on the undetermined segment scope, not on safety.

Undetermined changes the amount and the outcome, so it goes to a person [RD-2][RD-5]. No rider-named stop exists, so RD-3(a) does not apply [RD-3].

The complete timestamped chat [F11] holds only the 18:42 proposal [F9] and the 18:43 reply [F10]; no rider message before the 19:03 start approves this segment, and the driver's post-trip statement [F12] is not rider consent (G11). With no RD-4 incident [F15] and no rider-named stop [RD-3], the segment is an unexempted detour under RD-1 and refundable under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2][RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted as arithmetic only: extra km feed the metered fare ($14.64 billed, F5/F8), but RD-2 refunds only unexempted segments' extra_km, not the headline +10.4 km of F1 [RD-2].

Partly rejected: the second segment does rest on the driver's own admission [F12][RD-5], but the assertion that F3 is undetermined and therefore carries no refund is wrong on the consequence - an undetermined finding that changes the amount escalates rather than caps the recovery [F3][F9][F10][RD-2].
The rate derivation is accepted ($43.64 / 30.95 km = $1.4100/km [F8]; 4.78 x $1.4100 = $6.74 [F4][F5]) but the amount cannot be fixed while F3 is undetermined [RD-2].
Accepted as fact, with the consequence that no flag issues: route disputes upheld in 90 days = 0 [F18], so RD-6's condition is unmet [RD-6].

Rejected: reading 'Sure, your call.' [F10] against the driver's named-road proposal [F9], the agreement is to a named road rather than general faster-route authority, and no record ties this segment to it, so the exemption does not follow [F3][F9][F10][RD-5].
Rejected: both expressways are at band 4 (30-39 km/h) [F13][F14], not band 1-2, and no incident was recorded [F15], so RD-4 exempts neither segment [RD-4].
The concession is accepted, but it does not reach F3: driver-side statements are not consent and settle nothing about the first component of RD-1's per-segment review [F12][F15][RD-1][RD-4].
